simple.meaning: אָחוּ (ʼâchûw) is a Hebrew word meaning “a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אָחוּ (H260) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 41:2, with occurrences in Genesis, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָחוּ (H260) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אָחוּ (H260) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אָחוּ (ʼâchûw) / H260 is traced through Genesis 41:2, Genesis 41:18, Job 8:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile)
definitions.full: H260. achu אָחוּ : noun masculine Job 8:11 collective reeds, rushes (Aramaic אַחְוָא , originally Egyptian, compare demotic axu from axa be green , see Eb AG & BB Mos. 338 ; Wied Sammlung 16 ) Gen 41:2 , 18 (E) Job 8:11 ; also Hosea 13:15 where read אָחִים plural for אֲחָוִים (compare AW), or from a parallel form [ אָחֶה ], see De Compl. Var. 23 f . אַחְוָה see חוה .
